verdict.rationale: Circle's Wallets APIs let a developer create one or more wallets per user, which gives each customer a dedicated onchain address, and webhooks notify on resource state changes. The evidence never frames these as deposit addresses or virtual accounts for attributing incoming payments, and never describes reconciliation behavior. Missing for 10: explicit per-customer deposit-address or named virtual-account documentation, inbound-payment attribution or reconciliation metadata, fiat virtual account support, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, incoming funds are attributable — named virtual accounts or dedicated deposit addresses per customer so reconciliation knows who paid without manual matching

citations.quote: Creates a challenge for user initialization and creates one or more wallets.
you get APIs to create wallets, sign transactions, and authorize actions
